title: Quickstart sparkline pipeline & output cards for embeddings + rerank
creator: Lena Cho
description: Purpose: deliver a compact, developer-focused quickstart visual kit for Embeddings + Rerank that can be used across the docs quickstart, in-app console quickstarter, and marketing one-pagers. Deliverables include a horizontal 'sparkline' pipeline diagram showing time/cost impact per stage, a set of interactive-looking sample output cards (JSON + human-readable rerank output), and 2 screenshot compositions for docs and console placement. Goal is to reduce time-to-first-success: engineers should be able to read the visual, copy the minimal code snippet, and see example outputs in the playground within 2 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity horizontal sparkline pipeline SVG (desktop & mobile variants) exported in SVG and 2 PNG sizes
3 responsive sample output card designs: compact code + sample JSON, verbose human-readable rerank, and combined console screenshot
Microcopy for each pipeline stage (ingest -> embed -> index -> query -> rerank -> serve) with latency and cost callouts
Design annotated with responsive rules, color tokens, and accessibility contrast checks (AA)
Assets uploaded to Drive + Figma file updated; PM and ENG sign-off recorded
A minimal in-doc screenshot (1024x512) and a console mock (1280x720) produced for release notes

design_notes: Sparkline approach: use a stacked sparkline where each stage shows relative latency as a section of the line; annotate median and p95 as small callouts.
Color tokens: use brand-primary for embed stage, neutral-700 for index, accent-amber for rerank cost callout. Provide light/dark token palette in the Figma file.
Microcopy: Keep stage captions to 3 words max. Example: 'Embed (128d)', 'Index (annoyance: shard)'. Provide short explainer tooltip text for each stage in the design annotations.
Responsive rules: pipeline compresses to stacked vertical list below 640px; sample cards collapse to a single column.
Screenshot guidelines: console mock should include rounded card, non-sensitive sample data, and a visible 'Try in Playground' CTA. Use sandbox datasets only.
